correctness.rationale: An anchored unimodular translation identity gives F'(1+)=volume exactly. Replacing global-range-constrained F by a product of blockwise range-constrained cube volumes changes F(1+epsilon) only by O(N^2 epsilon^2), so derivatives agree. Differentiating the exact block factors proves the heterogeneous formula for every k,n_i,t_i. Elementary symmetric expansion and strictly positive transfer difference prove strict Schur-concavity for 0<t<1, including k=2 and singleton blocks; substitution gives extremal ratio asymptotic. Independently implemented Ehrhart-counting corroborated 20 rational-volume instances, and 5350 balancing transfers were checked. These finite tests are not used as proof of universal claims.

value.rationale: Continuous anchored-coordinate volume is a natural geometric invariant of a family of finite-dimensional Lipschitz dual balls; the result determines it for all cluster sizes and heterogeneous radii rather than a fixed finite table. Strict balancing compares every integer partition for common short radii and reveals reversal relative to the lengthened within-class metric regime, with a sharp polynomial dimension dependence. It resolves a motivated exact invariant and natural extremal ordering without claiming downstream applications.
